urgent_card.title: Get help now if you're worried
urgent_card.body: Call 999 or go to A&E if your child has stopped breathing or is struggling to breathe, turns blue or grey, cannot be woken, has a fit, has a rash that doesn't fade when you press a glass on it, or is under 3 months with a temperature of 38°C or more (39°C or more at 3 to 6 months). If you're worried about anything else or don't know what to do, call NHS 111 or use 111 online. Trust your instincts: you know your child best.
urgent_card.signpost: 999 for emergencies · NHS 111 for urgent advice

distress_card.title: You don't have to manage this alone
distress_card.body: It sounds like things are really hard right now. Your health visitor and GP support parents too, not just babies, so please tell them how you're feeling. If you feel you might harm yourself or your child, call 999 or go to A&E. For urgent mental health support, call NHS 111 and choose the mental health option, or call Samaritans free on 116 123 at any time.
distress_card.signpost: Health visitor or GP · NHS 111 (mental health option) · Samaritans 116 123 · 999 in an emergency

medication_card.title: Medicines and doses
medication_card.body: This app can't advise on medicines or doses. A pharmacist can tell you which medicines suit your child's age and weight and how much to give, or you can ask your GP or NHS 111.

disclaimer: This is general information, not medical advice. If you're worried about your child, talk to your health visitor or GP.
